name: NOVA
headline: Shopping, with a point of view.
summary: An editorial fashion app that connects discovery, product selection, saved pieces and a complete demo checkout.
teaser: A connected shopping experience. With a style of its own.
roleDetail: Mobile implementation, connected shopping flows, bilingual interfaces and an inspectable engineering architecture.
contributions: Built browsing, product variants, wishlist, bag and demo checkout flows.
Implemented English and Arabic experiences, including right-to-left layouts.
Connected guest and account sessions through Firebase adapters.
Implemented the Fold identity across native icons, splash and Flutter launch motion.
flows: Discover
Editorial home, categories, search, product details, sizes and colors.
Make it yours
Save pieces, build a bag, update quantities and apply promotions.
Complete the journey
Address, delivery, sandbox payment, review and a demo order receipt.
engineering: Account boundaries
Account-scoped state and adapter tests guard against retaining another account’s bag or late results.
Reliable demo checkout
Idempotent order saving and explicit sandbox payment verification separate a browser return from payment success.
Inspectable delivery
Feature-first Clean Architecture, repository adapters, Flutter tests and Firebase emulator checks are documented in the public project.
boundary: A portfolio demo with sample catalog content and sandbox payments. No real purchases. Product photography and third-party marks are illustrative; no affiliation is implied.

video.caption: A 50-second walkthrough recorded in the actual Flutter app. The public cut excludes address entry.

name: Brees
headline: A clearer view of everyday money.
summary: A navigable personal-finance experience connecting onboarding, accounts, transactions, budgets and financial insights.
teaser: From the first account to the bigger financial picture.
roleDetail: Figma analysis, UI reconstruction, navigation, interaction, animation, architecture, data mapping, automated testing, visual QA and CI.
contributions: Translated the Brees Figma Community product flow into Flutter.
Connected authentication, dashboard, transactions, budgets and insight journeys.
Separated presentation, use cases, repository contracts, data sources and transport.
Added automated visual QA, release builds and portfolio delivery.
flows: Get started
Launch motion, onboarding, account setup, sign-up and recovery states.
Understand the money
Balances, account detail, recent activity and transaction filtering.
Plan ahead
Budget setup, active budget states and a multi-screen insight story.
engineering: Visual consistency
A documented 60-state harness captures Flutter runtime output and compares it with stored design references.
Replaceable infrastructure
Feature and domain boundaries keep the interface independent of transport and data-source choices.
Release discipline
The project workflow runs analysis, automated tests, visual QA and a release APK build.
boundary: An independent engineering showcase based on the Brees Figma Community UI kit. The original product design is credited to that kit. This is a demo, not a live banking service.

name: OverDeal
headline: Ideas meet opportunity.
summary: A mobile platform for presenting ideas and projects, connecting project owners with people interested in new opportunities.
teaser: An original Flutter delivery, now a published product.
roleDetail: Developed the original mobile version: interfaces, user journeys, REST API integration, state and data handling, bilingual support and maintainable structure.
contributions: Implemented the original mobile UI and connected user journeys.
Integrated REST APIs and managed application data and state.
Supported Arabic, English and right-to-left layouts.
Delivered an organized Flutter foundation for continued development.
flows: Explore opportunities
Browse ideas and projects with structured details.
Present an idea
Enter project information through a guided submission flow.
Manage requests
Review incoming and outgoing requests and manage the account.
engineering: API-driven flows
The original delivery connected Flutter screens to REST APIs with application state and data handling.
Bilingual experience
Arabic and English support included right-to-left layouts.
Clear handover boundary
Another team made later updates for the product owner after the original version was delivered.
boundary: The app belongs to its owner. My contribution covers the original mobile version; later changes by another team are not attributed to me. Store images show the published listing and may include those later changes.

name: HealthTrack
headline: Care, connected across the journey.
summary: A Flutter healthcare showcase connecting specialty discovery, doctor appointments, scheduling and medical records.
teaser: One connected care journey. A carefully separated data layer.
roleDetail: Translated a Figma Community healthcare UI system into reusable Flutter screens, connected product journeys and a replaceable repository/data-source boundary.
contributions: Mapped the source UI system into a tested catalog of Flutter routes.
Connected doctor discovery, scheduling, appointment management and medical records.
Implemented session changes through a deterministic local data adapter.
Added navigation regression tests, data-layer tests and automated quality checks.
flows: Find care
Explore specialties, doctor lists, profiles and favorites.
Book an appointment
Choose a date and time, review payment screens and appointment details.
Keep track
Manage appointment states and add records within the demo session.
engineering: UI and data separation
Screens use HealthRepository and HealthDataSource boundaries; the current adapter uses local session data with simulated latency.
Navigation resilience
Regression coverage includes Favorites → Back → Home when there is no Navigator pop history.
Reusable product structure
Shared widgets support repeated specialty layouts while a route catalog test preserves the intended screen coverage.
boundary: Engineering showcase using local session data. It is not a live healthcare service or a production medical backend. The original Figma Community UI kit is the design reference, not my original visual design.

name: Madow
headline: An invitation to every occasion.
summary: An Arabic-first invitation experience for choosing an occasion, exploring designs, selecting a package and entering event details.
roleDetail: Shaped the multi-step invitation experience, Arabic-first interface, invitation examples and dedicated product screens.
contributions: Built the guided occasion, package and template selection journey.
Created Arabic RTL layouts and typography.
Organized wedding, graduation, birthday and newborn invitation examples.
Added home, template gallery, preview, package and order-history screens.
flows: Choose the occasion
Wedding, graduation, birthday and newborn categories.
Find a design
Browse templates and review the invitation preview.
Make it personal
Choose a package and continue to the event details.
engineering: Arabic at the center
Layout, navigation and typography support the right-to-left product experience.
Guided decisions
The flow separates occasion, design and package choices into focused steps.
boundary: A presentation/demo project. The public repository contains presentation material, not Flutter source. Online services, payment processing and backend behavior are not represented as production features. No shareable APK is currently linked.

name: Qurani
headline: A quiet space for daily practice.
summary: A Flutter Islamic app bringing together prayer times, Quran and tafsir, adhkar, Qibla direction and Hijri dates.
teaser: Quran, prayer times and daily remembrance.
roleDetail: The public project presentation identifies Hussein Abozina as the developer. Application source is maintained privately.
contributions: Developed the Flutter app presented through the public Qurani showcase.
Provided a public Android APK and app screenshots for hands-on review.
flows: Read
Quran reading and tafsir within the app.
Stay on time
Location-based prayer times, calculation methods and prayer notification controls.
Return every day
Morning and evening adhkar, Forty Nawawi, Qibla direction and Hijri dates.
engineering: Device-centered features
The documented product combines location-based prayer calculations, notifications and a Qibla compass.
Reviewable build
An Android release and real app screenshots provide public product evidence while the source remains private.
boundary: A public Android APK is available through the presentation repository. No app-store publication is claimed. More detailed architecture and ownership breakdown are not documented in the public source.

name: Messaging platform
headline: Engineering the foundations of conversation.
summary: An evolving messaging project with a Flutter client, a NestJS backend and PostgreSQL. The public repository records completed checkpoints and the remaining integration work.
teaser: Flutter meets a documented messaging backend.
roleDetail: The repository documents Flutter modernization, backend foundations, API contracts, architecture decisions and CI. The product is still under development.
contributions: Organized the Flutter client into feature-first auth and chat layers.
Documented and implemented backend auth, users, direct conversations and durable text messages.
Added read pointers, sender-owned edit/delete behavior and backend E2E verification.
Recorded realtime contracts separately from completed implementation.
flows: Identity
Backend authentication, user profiles and discovery.
Durable messages
Direct conversations, text persistence, read pointers, editing and soft deletion.
Mobile transition
The current Flutter app still runs its legacy Firebase chat behavior.
engineering: Durable state first
The documented backend uses PostgreSQL, explicit migrations and REST-based durable message behavior.
Safe retries and authorization
Sender/client-message idempotency, conversation membership checks and reply isolation are documented.
An honest integration boundary
The reviewed project checkpoint says custom Flutter REST/realtime adapters and the new multi-conversation UI are not implemented yet.
boundary: In development. The reviewed checkpoint is dated September 30, 2026. Realtime/WebSocket transport is planned, not integrated into the active backend chain. No production deployment, complete new UI or live realtime demo is claimed.
